findings.statement: CXCR2, the top-ranked candidate, is almost entirely a neutrophil transcript in Gubatan 2026 (neutrophil share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]). Smillie 2019 did not capture neutrophils and assigns it to T/NK cells, so the attribution does not replicate there (replicated=false; second dataset says myeloid). In bulk the change shrinks from [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; unadjusted_log2fc=2.5984] to [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409], still significant, so the verdict is partly_composition: the bulk signal is mostly neutrophil influx, with a smaller residual that may reflect over-correction.

CXCL8 is made mainly by neutrophils in inflamed mucosa (neutrophil share [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]), while Smillie 2019 attributes it to macrophages and a second dataset agrees on myeloid lineage. After composition adjustment it is no longer significant ([gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0527]), verdict composition. It behaves as a marker of myeloid and neutrophil influx; this is not proof of pure influx because adjustment can over-correct.

IL1B is myeloid in both datasets, but neutrophils carry a large share of its inflamed-tissue transcripts ([gene=IL1B; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.702]). Its bulk increase does not survive composition adjustment ([gene=IL1B; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0735]), verdict composition, so it is mainly a cell-influx marker; the caveat on over-correction applies.

S100A8 is a myeloid transcript replicated across datasets, with most inflamed-mucosa transcripts coming from neutrophils ([gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909]). It keeps a significant adjusted change ([gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.9231]), verdict partly_composition: a neutrophil and monocyte burden marker with some within-tissue induction.

CD274 (PD-L1) is spread across lineages (myeloid dominant in Smillie, replicated in the second dataset) with a large neutrophil share in Gubatan ([gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]). It retains a significant adjusted change ([gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978]), verdict partly_composition: a mixed influx and tissue induction signal, not a clean single-cell target.

IDO1 is myeloid (macrophages and DC1, replicated in the second dataset) and not a neutrophil gene (neutrophil share [gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.072]); in Gubatan enterocytes are also a top source. The adjusted change stays significant ([gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505]), verdict partly_composition, which points to induction inside the tissue.

MMP1 is a stromal product, replicated in the second dataset, led by inflammatory fibroblasts in inflamed mucosa (cluster share [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.531]). The change keeps strong significance after adjustment ([gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]), verdict partly_composition, so it is a fibroblast-state change inside the tissue rather than neutrophil influx.

CHI3L1 is mainly an inflammatory-fibroblast gene (cluster share [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.652]), replicated in the second dataset, although neutrophil states also contribute in Gubatan. The adjusted change remains large ([gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967]), verdict partly_composition, supporting a tissue-intrinsic fibroblast signal.

DUOX2 is epithelial (enterocytes and immature enterocytes), replicated in the second dataset, with an epithelial lineage share of [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947] and almost no neutrophil contribution. Its adjusted change stays significant ([gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]), verdict partly_composition: an epithelial-intrinsic induction and a sign of epithelial stress.

OSMR is stromal (lineage share [gene=OSMR; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.907], replicated in the second dataset), spread over several fibroblast clusters. The adjusted change is small but still significant ([gene=OSMR; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.2528]), verdict partly_composition, so most of the bulk rise tracks cell composition and only a modest part is intrinsic.

caveats: No candidate in the tested set received the verdict intrinsic; most were partly_composition, and CXCL8 and IL1B were composition.
Composition adjustment can over-correct, because lineage scores also rise when resident cells activate; losing significance is not proof of pure influx, and keeping it is the stronger statement.
Smillie 2019 lacks neutrophils, so neutrophil-derived genes (CXCR2, CXCR1, CXCL8, S100A8, AQP9) are attributed to other immune cells there; use the Gubatan neutrophil shares for them.
Shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance; dissociation protocols enrich some fractions.
CXCR1, AQP9, CXCL1, MMP3, LCN2 and SLC26A2 were only screened for neutrophil share (CXCR1 and AQP9 are mostly neutrophil, SLC26A2 almost none); no composition analysis was run for them.
Spatial context (Xenium) was not examined within the call budget.
